records.title: Advances in understanding contact electrification via DFT and molecular dynamics simulations
records.description: Contact electrification is a known phenomenon, yet its underlying mechanism remains unclear. This Review discusses how density functional theory and molecular dynamics are used to study the electron-transfer, ion-transfer and material-transfer processes that can occur when materials come into contact.

records.title: Dynamic interactions at active sites in electrocatalysis
records.description: Dynamic interactions among active centres, functional motifs, intermediates and microenvironments define active sites as an ensemble in electrocatalysis. This Review classifies these interactions, explains their entanglement and spatiotemporal resolution through complementary approaches, and outlines operando-guided catalyst design.

records.title: From biology to boron chemistry
records.description: Ahead of his 65th birthday, Holger Braunschweig, Head and Chair of Inorganic Chemistry at the University of Würzburg, discussed his life in science.

records.title: When shape changes fate
Strategies for the intracellular synthesis of bioactive molecules in living cells
records.description: Intracellular synthesis is emerging as a powerful strategy to generate bioactive molecules directly in living cells, offering opportunities to control where and when biological activity is produced. This Review discusses bond-forming reactions that generate biologically relevant pharmacophores and fluorophores in cells, focusing on metal-catalysed, bioorthogonal, light-promoted and endogenous-stimulus-driven approaches.

records.title: Discussions with the gene editor
records.description: Ahead of his 45th birthday, Feng Zhang, James and Patricia Poitras Professor of Neuroscience at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, discussed his life in science.

records.title: Chemistry at a tipping point
records.description: Chemistry is evolving from predominantly manual experimentation towards increasingly automated and data-driven discovery, incorporating sustainability and integrating other disciplines. Chemistry education must respond to these changes in industry, research and society or we will watch the educational pipeline continue to decline.

records.title: Operando and multiscale insights into the solid electrolyte interphase in lithium-mediated nitrogen reduction
records.description: This Review examines how the dynamic solid electrolyte interphase governs lithium-mediated ammonia synthesis and highlights complementary operando, in situ and multiscale characterization strategies to resolve the composition, structure and evolution of the former, guiding rational solid electrolyte interphase design for improved efficiency, selectivity and durability.

records.title: Distinguishing single-site from single-atom catalysts
records.description: Single-atom catalysis has triggered an enormous research boom. However, inconsistent terminology is widely encountered in the literature, particularly for single-atom versus single-site catalysts. By clarifying the origins of these catalysts, and distinguishing their criteria and structural boundaries, this Comment proposes standardized characterization benchmarks and writing norms to unify terminology.

records.title: The concept of aromaticity after 200 years of benzene
records.description: The lack of a unified framework for aromaticity often prevents cross-disciplinary comprehension. By summarizing fundamental concepts and highlighting recent developments in excited-state, 3D and metallaaromaticity, this Review bridges these conceptual gaps to foster a holistic understanding.

records.title: Chemistry is vital for growth
records.description: Chemistry is a strategically vital UK strength and underpins many of the sectors identified as priorities for future growth. Yet despite its economic significance and continued demand for the skills it supplies, chemistry is facing structural pressures that need serious attention from universities, funders and governments across the UK.

records.title: Photocatalytic VOC removal
records.description: Mahshab Sheraz explains how a custom photocatalytic column reactor integrates capturing volatile organic compounds, light-driven filter regeneration and humidity effects, enabling realistic continuous-flow evaluation of reusable filter membranes for cleaner indoor air.

records.title: Interfacial hydrogen transfer for heterogeneous catalysis
records.description: The formation and interfacial transfer of reactive hydrogen species (H + , H· and H δ − ) is crucial for various reactions and systems, such as hydrogen evolution, hydrogenation and fuel cells. Understanding these transfer pathways is key when designing next-generation catalysts capable of precisely controlling hydrogen dynamics.

records.title: A new angle on dopamine–membrane interactions
records.description: Dopamine is usually thought of as a ligand that binds to a receptor. However, a recent study demonstrated that dopamine also dynamically interacts with a lipid bilayer by binding to the membrane’s surface and bending the acyl chains of the lipids on the outer leaflet.

records.title: Structural evolution of ionizable lipids for nucleic acid delivery
records.description: Ionizable lipids represent central components in nucleic acid therapeutics. This Review outlines their structural evolution, design strategies and emerging functions while highlighting next-generation principles and translational perspectives that may guide precision RNA therapeutics in regenerative medicines.

records.title: Mechanistic questions in aqueous–organic chemistry
records.description: Aqueous–organic reaction media contain dynamic colloidal structures that strongly influence reactivity and selectivity yet remain difficult to characterize. This Perspective discusses outstanding mechanistic questions, evaluates available analytical tools and identifies routes towards a predictive framework for reaction development in water.

records.title: One molecule, two clocks
records.description: This article highlights a newly developed chemically fuelled logic gate whereby a single porphyrin dye is driven by two independent enzyme reactions, one setting its colour and the other its fluorescence. Because the two outputs recover on separately tunable timescales, the system produces a programmable delay of up to about 23 minutes between them, letting the researchers control not just whether a signal appears but when.

records.title: Static apparatus for vapour pressure measurements
records.description: Bruno Pinheiro explains the workings of their custom-made apparatus for measuring vapour pressures with high accuracy within large pressure and temperature ranges.

records.title: Time for o-chem to level up
records.description: A 2026 public survey suggests that organic chemistry (o-chem) remains underappreciated and misunderstood in the modern era — is it finally time to take action?

records.title: Permeable by design
records.description: Mycobacterial drug discovery is held back by the challenge of limited compound penetration across the mycomembrane. An experimentally enabled machine-learning approach identifies permeability-promoting molecular features that could help guide medicinal chemistry toward more permeable antibacterial candidates.

records.title: An expert in creating complex structures
records.description: Ahead of her 65th birthday, Margaret Brimble, Distinguished Professor and Director of Medicinal Chemistry at the University of Auckland, discussed her life in science.

records.title: Watching ice nucleation in real-time
records.description: Devendra Pal explains how their custom-made ice nucleation chamber works, yielding data on nucleation itself as well as particle sizes, phases, and morphologies in an effort to understand cloud formation and its impact on atmospheric chemistry.

records.title: Molten salt electrochemistry for next-generation batteries
records.description: This Review discusses molten salt electrochemistry for energy storage systems, covering electrolyte chemistry, charge storage, cell configurations and materials innovations, and points to future opportunities in cathode design, ion-selective membranes and advanced molten salt systems.

records.title: Subcellular photochemistry for precision spatial protein targeting
records.description: Conventional drug design lacks the spatial control needed for the selective targeting of mislocalized proteins, a pervasive phenomenon with diseases. This Perspective discusses how subcellular photochemistry combined with a prodrug approach can target those conserved proteins precisely.

records.title: Targeting soluble misfolded oligomers in anti-amyloid research
records.description: This Review surveys emerging chemical and biophysical tools for detection, characterization and intervention of soluble misfolded oligomers. These small oligomers are considered the main disease-causing species for amyloid diseases. Targeting these oligomers is highlighted as a promising research direction.

records.title: Atmospheric chemistry of volatile methyl siloxanes
records.description: Volatile methyl siloxanes are synthetic compounds that readily partition to the atmosphere and have been a focus of policy debates. This Review discusses advances in understanding the atmospheric chemistry, lifetimes and abundancies of these compounds and their oxidation products.

records.title: The automated red pen
records.description: Large language models can grade a stack of chemistry assignments before the kettle has boiled. Whether we should let them depends less on speed than on purpose. Before an AI marker influences grades, it should be validated like an analytical method, with defined limits, quality control and a route to appeal.

records.title: Missing marks made visible
records.description: RNA modifications shape function but are hard to localize. A recent study used an enzyme-based fluorescent method to image queuine-deficient tRNAs in cells.

records.title: The past, present and future of self-driving laboratories
records.description: Self-driving laboratories integrate automation, robotics and artificial intelligence to accelerate chemical discovery. This Review charts their evolution from bespoke systems to interoperable platforms, highlighting challenges in scalability, generalizability and data provenance, and outlining pathways towards networked, trustworthy infrastructures enabling collective scientific superintelligence.

records.title: Making sense of hydrogen evolution
records.description: Adrian Lathouwers explains how a custom glass photoreactor, which integrates an amperometric microsensor, enables controlled and reproducible hydrogen evolution measurements for assessing photocatalytic activity.

records.title: Supramolecular self-assembly by layering orthogonality to program identity, connectivity and conformation
records.description: The supramolecular self-assembly of topologically complex architectures is governed by the interplay of many reversible interaction types. This Review highlights strategies and limitations of combining different classes of interactions that must act orthogonally to direct structure. DCC, dynamic-covalent chemistry.

records.title: Physicochemical processes in evaporation-based perovskite LEDs
records.description: This Perspective presents a chemistry-driven framework linking physicochemical processes to system-level control in evaporation-based perovskite light-emitting diodes. We provide actionable guidelines for reproducible deposition and scalable device manufacturing.

records.title: Mathematics and mentorship make a recipe for success
records.description: Ahead of his 80th birthday, Isiah M. Warner, Boyd Professor Emeritus in the Department of Chemistry at Louisiana State University, discussed his life in science.

records.title: Sequence-defined polymers for predictable gene delivery
records.description: Polymer vectors for non-viral gene delivery are typically inefficient and heterogeneous. This Review explores how sequence-defined polymers, advanced synthesis, imaging and computational design can enable precise, reproducible and programmable polymer systems for efficient and clinically translatable nucleic acid delivery.

records.title: Precision chemical engineering of dendrimers for nucleic acid delivery
records.description: Dendrimers offer precise and tunable platforms for nucleic acids delivery. This Review outlines advances in dendrimer engineering for the delivery of diverse nucleic acids, highlighting their applications in therapeutics, vaccines and genome editing. Translational challenges including manufacturing, safety and regulatory considerations are also discussed, with perspectives to accelerate clinical translation.

records.title: Bridging stimulus-responsive and dissipative peptide assemblies to build complex interactive biomaterials
records.description: Self-assembling peptides offer programmable routes to biomaterials with dynamic behaviour. Here, we compare stimulus-responsive and dissipative peptide assemblies, outline their design principles, and highlight strategies to integrate them, enabling complex, interactive biomaterials that emulate the non-equilibrium functions of living systems.

records.title: Unlocking the potential of plastic in e-waste
records.description: Plastic is a rapidly growing, yet overlooked, resource of electronic waste. It should be redefined as a chemically rich feedstock for high-value materials, rather than a disposal challenge. Realizing this potential requires advances in conversion technologies, system-level process integration, and policy frameworks enabling circular materials use and resource-efficient value chains.

records.title: Devising a divisome for synthetic cells
records.description: Cell division consists of three elementary steps: symmetry breaking, membrane constriction and abscission. Here, we review current strategies for achieving these steps in synthetic cells, assessing their successes and limitations with a view to integrating them within a divisome for synthetic cells.

records.title: Feeling the force
records.description: Maria Kaeek explains the workings of a custom-built surface forces balance, a tool capable of measuring the van der Waals forces between two atomically smooth surfaces just a few nanometres apart with an unrivalled resolution.

records.title: Dyeing and drying, but not dying
records.description: In 2015, Freitag and colleagues serendipitously discovered that dye-sensitized solar cells with copper-complex electrolytes continued to function after drying out, performing as well as their liquid predecessors. This launched a new class of sold-state devices, ‘zombie’ cells, with power-conversion efficiencies over 10% in sunlight and approaching 40% under indoor light.

records.title: Tales of total synthesis
records.description: Ahead of his 80th birthday, Kyriacos Costa (K. C.) Nicolaou, Harry C. and Olga K. Wiess Professor of Chemistry at Rice University, spoke about his career in science.

records.title: A trigger that feeds itself
records.description: Most reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive prodrug linkers consume the oxidant that triggers them. A new self-immolative linker instead regenerates it, coupling drug release to signal amplification in one component.

records.title: Making chemistry sing with AI
records.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) opens up classroom creativity, enabling students and instructors to generate chemistry-themed songs with ease. This playful approach may enhance engagement, support memorization of complex concepts, and prompt critical reflection on the role of generative AI in education.

records.title: Advances in electrochemical peptide synthesis and modification
records.description: Electrochemistry is a powerful strategy for precise, tunable and sustainable synthesis that is now broadening the landscape of synthetic peptide chemistry. This Review summarizes electrochemical strategies for peptide synthesis and residue-specific modifications, highlighting opportunities for the efficient preparation of bioactive and structurally diverse peptides.

records.title: Publisher Correction: Reprogramming CO 2 reduction through interfacial water
Hydrogen generation promoted by single-atom-based thermochemical catalysts
records.description: This Review details the fundamentals of single-atom catalysts for H 2 -generation technologies. We discuss the different reaction pathways, CO x by-products and their potential eliminations, CO x -free pathways, catalyst structure–performance relationships and the techno-economics of the different processes, including cost factors and scalability.

records.title: The phonon map of molecular qubits
records.description: Molecular spin qubits are of great interest for quantum technologies due to their tunability, scalability, reproducibility and potential for room-temperature operation. While electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy is often used to study molecular qubit coherence, this has recently been paired with inelastic neutron scattering to study qubit decoherence.

records.title: Building a neuroinclusive lab
records.description: Chemistry laboratories are abundant with sensory stimuli. This Comment explores the impact of sensory overload on scientists working in these environments and offers suggestions to facilitate neuroinclusive laboratories.

records.title: Author Correction: NMR spectrometers that go places others can’t.
A career of taking biological species for a spin
records.description: Ahead of his 70th birthday, Adriaan (Ad) Bax, Distinguished Investigator at the National Institutes of Health (NIH), spoke about his career in science.

records.title: Alternating current magnetorheometer for real-time investigations
records.description: Richa Chaudhary explains how a custom alternating current magnetorheometer enables real-time rheological measurements of, for example, polymers and electromagnetic materials during exposure to alternating magnetic fields. Such measurements are not possible with conventional magnetorheometers.

records.title: Author Correction: Why university-level chemistry education in the UK is under threat
NMR spectrometers that go places others can’t
records.description: Addressing global challenges like climate change and pollution requires the development of advanced materials. To succeed, material scientists must use a diverse array of characterization tools. While often overshadowed by high-field systems, bench-top time-domain NMR offers unique advantages that could be instrumental in accelerating the development of sustainable material solutions.

records.title: Why university-level chemistry education in the UK is under threat
records.description: University-level chemistry education in the UK is facing mounting pressures that threaten its long-term viability. Without decisive intervention, we risk losing the scientific talent and capacity needed to retain the UK’s position as a leader in innovation.

records.title: Spatiotemporal analysis of reactive oxygen species using specific activity-based sensing fluorescent imaging probes
records.description: Oxidative stress arises from reactive oxygen species that are essential for signalling yet harmful when uncontrolled. Fluorescence imaging enables real-time, sensitive, organelle-level reactive oxygen species detection, and this Review outlines design principles for developing reliable probes to advance biological and medical research. MAO, monoamine oxidase; MPO, myeloperoxidase; NO, nitric oxide; NOS, nitric oxide synthase; SOD, superoxide dismutase.

records.title: Listening to the Accessible Audio Periodic Table
records.description: Every student deserves to be able to independently explore periodic trends in a chemistry course; with the Accessible Audio Periodic Table, students can now access a free tool that incorporates Universal Design for Learning (UDL) principles and accessibility to allow exploration through sound and sight.

records.title: Diversifying chemical reactions in solid oxide electrochemical cells
records.description: Nearly 40 years ago, solid oxide electrochemical cells began to evolve from supplying energy into versatile chemical reactors. Since then, breakthroughs in cell design and demonstrations of efficient value-added chemical reactions led to the exploration of how, for example, interface engineering enables more efficient and sustainable valorization reactions at reduced temperatures.

records.title: The path to understanding how reactions work and fail
records.description: Ahead of his 60th birthday, Guy Lloyd-Jones, Forbes Professor of Organic Chemistry at the University of Edinburgh, spoke about his career in science.

records.title: Fluorine-free super-repellency to water and organic liquids
records.description: Fluorine-free super-repellent materials provide sustainable and scalable alternatives to fluorinated counterparts by using re-entrant architectures or pairing non-fluorinated surface chemistries with hierarchical roughness. This Review highlights fundamental design principles, theoretical frameworks, emerging applications and future research opportunities.

records.title: Dialling in the heat
records.description: Smita Dasari explains how a radio-frequency heating apparatus can be used to, for example, cure polymers as well as probe electrical conductivities and dielectric properties of various other materials ranging from epoxies to carbon fibres and MXenes.

records.title: Light-driven reforming of methane through photothermal catalysis
records.description: This Review reframes photothermal catalytic methane reforming as a three-driving-force system, revealing how coupled photocarriers, heat (or phonons) and gradient fields govern reaction pathways, kinetics and selectivity, in addition to creating dynamic microenvironments for efficient solar-driven syngas production exemplified by dry reforming of methane.

records.title: A life researching the path to better polymers
records.description: Ahead of his 70th birthday, Takuzo Aida, Group Director at RIKEN and Distinguished University Professor at the University of Tokyo, discussed his research career.

records.title: The chemistry of magnetoelectric multiferroics
records.description: The development of ferroelectric (ferro)magnetic multiferroic materials is discussed from a chemist’s perspective, highlighting chemical contraindications, developments in solid-state chemistry that have yielded new multiferroics, chemical applications of multiferroic materials and open questions that await answers.

records.title: Polarity promotes power production
records.description: Thermoelectrochemical hydrogels can generate voltages as the temperature rises, which is often due to multiple, coupled transport mechanisms. Recent work shows how electrochemically tuning the chain-polarity can direct charge transport in hydrogels, highlighting how precise control of such chains can enhance thermoelectric performance.

records.title: Molecular rotor-based probes for protein monitoring in biomedical research
records.description: Fluorescent molecular rotor probes respond to microenvironmental changes in cells, enabling real-time, non-invasive detection of protein biomarkers in living cells, overcoming the limits of conventional approaches. They brighten upon target binding as a result of restricted intramolecular rotation and show promise for both diagnostics and research.

records.title: Chemical heterogeneity for battery materials
records.description: Materials science has long been shaped by the interplay between homogeneous and heterogeneous designs. Homogeneous battery materials offer predictability but face inherent trade-offs. Therefore, emerging research has begun to explore chemical heterogeneity to overcome these challenges and enhance the electrochemical properties of batteries.

records.title: Photochemical, electrochemical and electrophotochemical C−N bond-forming cross-coupling reactions
records.description: This Review encompasses recent developments in photochemical, electrochemical and electrophotochemical C–N coupling reactions, focusing on metal-catalysed and metal-free methodologies under diverse activation conditions. It highlights sustainable and versatile synthetic strategies for C–N bond formation.

records.title: More than just a delivery system
records.description: Lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-encapsulated messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccines proved highly effective during the COVID-19 pandemic, but how their chemical components collectively program immune responses has remained incompletely understood. Now, new work shows that both mRNA cargo and LNP materials provide layered chemical signals that instruct vaccine immunity.

records.title: Making movies with ultra-fast pair distribution functions
records.description: Adam Sapnik details the importance of custom beamline detector setups at X-ray free electron lasers for ultra-fast scattering and pair distribution function measurements of various disordered and solution-phase systems.

records.title: Light-responsive DNA nanostructures
records.description: Light-responsive chemical modifications enable precise, stimuli-controlled reconfiguration of DNA nanostructures, enhancing stability, programmability and functional versatility. These advances expand applications in diagnostics, delivery, data storage and nanoscale engineering. Emerging design strategies and new photochemical tools driving the field forward are highlighted.

records.title: Reprogramming CO 2 reduction through interfacial water
records.description: Controlling the electrochemical interface can reshape catalytic pathways. By reorganizing interfacial water with polymeric cations, CO 2 reduction on Ag shifts from CO to formic acid, revealing the importance of solvent structure for tuning electrocatalytic selectivity.

records.title: Customizing abrasives with chemical additives
records.description: Arsalan Ahmad discusses how a viscoelastic matrix composed of polymer chains, embedded with hard particles, can be used to create a custom abrasive to smoothen surfaces, cut grooves, or map pressure-points on surfaces of materials.

records.title: Author Correction: Matter in ångström-scale two-dimensional confinement
Growing pains
records.description: To write this article, the authors, members of the International Women in Supramolecular Chemistry (WISC) network surveyed colleagues who care for older children about the challenges of integrating that role with their academic careers.

records.title: Synthetic methodologies for the chemical recycling of fluorocarbons
records.description: The fluorochemical industry is extensive, but fundamentally unsustainable. In this Review, we highlight synthetic methods for recycling fluorocarbons, with a focus on methods that can be applied for industrially relevant fluorochemicals including refrigerants and fluoropolymers.

records.title: Mapping a career in electron microscopy
records.description: Ahead of his 60th birthday, Paul A. Midgley, Professor of Materials Science at the University of Cambridge, discussed his life in science.

records.title: Enhancing chemical safety information for the future
records.description: High-quality chemical safety information is essential, but information is often fragmented, inconsistent and incomplete. As a result, users face unrealistic expectations in applying risk-based principles. This article highlights persistent challenges and urges stakeholders to improve access, accuracy and application of chemical safety data.

records.title: Quantum sieving from thermal desorption
records.description: Sibo Chetry explains how an ultrahigh-vacuum chamber with a cryostat and temperature-controlled sample stage can be used for quantum sieving by thermal desorption of an isotopic mixture.

records.title: Beyond ligase logic for proteolysis
records.description: Direct recruitment of target proteins is a ubiquitination-independent approach for protein degradation and provides an alternative approach to proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) for targeted protein degradation.

records.title: Enhancing the targeting ability of metal–organic frameworks in cancer therapy and diagnosis
records.description: This Review introduces methods for enhancing the targeting ability of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), reviews their applications when modified with different types of targeting molecules and provides guidance for the next-generation MOFs to achieve accurate cancer diagnosis and treatment.

records.title: Matter in ångström-scale two-dimensional confinement
records.description: Under confinement, matter shows different structures and behaviours, which are particularly pronounced at the ångström scale. This Review focuses on the new structures and properties of matter under such ångström-scale 2D confinement.

records.title: Catalytic droplets
records.description: A recent study showed peptides could self-assemble into catalytic droplets that could promote an aqueous aldol addition. This approach provides a proof of concept example of a droplet working as a reaction field to accelerate chemical reactions.

records.title: Tumour microenvironment in the surgical spotlight
records.description: Surgical tumour removal is often hindered by unclear margins. A recent study has developed a ‘spray on’ fluorescent probe system that rapidly stains and highlights tumour edges, enabling high contrast, real time margin detection that can be used directly in the surgical field.

records.title: Author Correction: Chemistry advances driving industrial carbon capture technologies
Understanding the degradation complexity of ultrahigh-energy lithium metal batteries
records.description: This Review discusses the lifespan failure chemistry of lithium metal batteries beyond 600 Wh kg −1 , highlighting the challenges in assessing active Li loss. We correlate material degradation, cell parameters, cell assembly and operating conditions to the overall performance and failure of a lithium metal battery.

records.title: Empowering the next generation of scientists
records.description: We are a group of graduate students from the University of California, Los Angeles who represent the Organization for Cultural Diversity in Science. In this Comment we describe a number of our initiatives to uplift and enrich the scientific community of which we are a part.

records.title: Carbon capture with COFs
records.description: A polyamine-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) overcomes traditional direct air capture limitations with rapid CO 2 adsorption kinetics and high capacity, offering a promising solution for efficient carbon capture and sustainable climate mitigation.

records.title: Foundation models for atomistic simulation of chemistry and materials
records.description: We examine the historical development and underlying principles of foundation models realized in language and vision, and propose how physics-infused machine learning interaction potentials could dramatically transform at scale to create transformative foundation models for chemistry and materials science.

records.title: Author Correction: Substitution and electrochemistry in layered oxide cathode materials for sodium-ion batteries
A call for chemical safety and sustainability
records.description: The Stockholm Declaration on Chemistry for the Future, launched during the Nobel Symposium in May 2025, aims to align research, education, industry, and governance with the goal of focusing the future of chemistry on safety and sustainability.

records.title: A conversation with a chemical biology pioneer
records.description: Ahead of his 70th birthday, Stuart Schreiber, Morris Loeb Research Professor at Harvard University, discussed his life in science.

records.title: Towards effective and ethical GenAI in chemistry education
records.description: In 2025, chemistry education research moved towards more mature and critical uses of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI). Recent studies show how GenAI can support visualization and learning of abstract chemical concepts, while highlighting the need for strong AI literacy to manage errors, ethics and misuse.

records.title: Substitution and electrochemistry in layered oxide cathode materials for sodium-ion batteries
records.description: The impact of atomic substitution in sodium-layered oxides and how substitutions affect the properties and performances of battery materials are discussed, with the aim of improving sodium-layered oxides and accelerating the commercialization of sodium-ion batteries.

records.title: Stories from the scientist who changed how we visualize proteins
records.description: Ahead of her 85th birthday, Jane Richardson, Professor of Biochemistry at Duke University, discussed her life in science from making her own telescope to developing the ribbon diagrams for the 3D structure of proteins.

records.title: Making chemistry compute with non-steady-state chemical dynamics
records.description: Non-steady-state chemical dynamics offer a powerful tool for neuromorphic computing by harnessing nonlinear, collective, and time-evolving behaviours. Coupled with frameworks such as reservoir computing, these systems enable trajectory-based information processing at the molecular scale through concepts from chemical kinetics and far-from-equilibrium dynamics.

records.title: The geopolitical future for chemistry
records.description: In an era of global transition, new frontiers in chemistry — from space mining to circular technologies — are poised to reshape global power. This Comment explores how future supply chains, strategic resources, and chemistry could define the next era of geopolitical competition.

records.title: First-principles approaches and concepts to simulate electrochemical interfaces
records.description: State-of-the-art approaches for modelling electrified solid–electrolyte interfaces are critically discussed, highlighting key challenges in incorporating thermodynamic open-boundary conditions, large electrostatic potentials and their dynamic fluctuations into realistic ab initio simulations.

records.title: Ion migration in perovskite solar cells
records.description: Ion migration plays a crucial role in perovskite solar cells. This Review covers its mechanisms, impact on device performance and degradation, measurement techniques, and emerging strategies towards controlling ion migration.

records.title: Programming DNA machines to move
records.description: The development of DNA-based machines is transforming fields such as drug delivery and biosensing. Here, design strategies are discussed and key performance metrics — speed, force generation, efficiency and autonomy — are examined to provide insights into the future of DNA nanotechnology.

records.title: Tin, Sn!
records.description: Time flies when you’re having fun, they say. And so it is that we welcome you to the 10th volume of Nature Reviews Chemistry .

records.title: Strengthening school–university collaborations
records.description: Chemistry is an experimental science that for many learners only comes alive in the laboratory. But specialized equipment is increasingly out of reach of school budgets. Strengthening school–university collaborations can help to bridge the gap.

records.title: Biomolecular coronas govern the environmental fate of metal–organic frameworks
records.description: Metal–organic frameworks are increasingly used in environmental technologies, whereby their biomolecular coronas determine their identity, transport, persistence and ecosystem effects. We argue that further research is needed to embed corona considerations into framework systems design and regulation, and we outline the minimal, actionable steps needed to achieve this.

records.title: Advances in understanding contact electrification via DFT and molecular dynamics simulations

This Review discusses how density functional theory and molecular dynamics are used to study the electron-transfer, ion-transfer and material-transfer processes that can occur when materials come into contact.

Because the two outputs recover on separately tunable timescales, the system produces a programmable delay of up to about 23 minutes between them, letting the researchers control not just whether a signal appears but when.

records.title: Static apparatus for vapour pressure measurements
records.description: Bruno Pinheiro explains the workings of their custom-made apparatus for measuring vapour pressures with high accuracy within large pressure and temperature ranges.

records.title: Time for o-chem to level up
records.description: A 2026 public survey suggests that organic chemistry (o-chem) remains underappreciated and misunderstood in the modern era — is it finally time to take action?

records.title: Permeable by design
records.description: Mycobacterial drug discovery is held back by the challenge of limited compound penetration across the mycomembrane. An experimentally enabled machine-learning approach identifies permeability-promoting molecular features that could help guide medicinal chemistry toward more permeable antibacterial candidates.

records.title: An expert in creating complex structures
records.description: Ahead of her 65th birthday, Margaret Brimble, Distinguished Professor and Director of Medicinal Chemistry at the University of Auckland, discussed her life in science.

records.title: Watching ice nucleation in real-time
records.description: Devendra Pal explains how their custom-made ice nucleation chamber works, yielding data on nucleation itself as well as particle sizes, phases, and morphologies in an effort to understand cloud formation and its impact on atmospheric chemistry.

records.title: Molten salt electrochemistry for next-generation batteries
records.description: This Review discusses molten salt electrochemistry for energy storage systems, covering electrolyte chemistry, charge storage, cell configurations and materials innovations, and points to future opportunities in cathode design, ion-selective membranes and advanced molten salt systems.

records.title: Subcellular photochemistry for precision spatial protein targeting
records.description: Conventional drug design lacks the spatial control needed for the selective targeting of mislocalized proteins, a pervasive phenomenon with diseases. This Perspective discusses how subcellular photochemistry combined with a prodrug approach can target those conserved proteins precisely.

records.title: Targeting soluble misfolded oligomers in anti-amyloid research
records.description: This Review surveys emerging chemical and biophysical tools for detection, characterization and intervention of soluble misfolded oligomers. These small oligomers are considered the main disease-causing species for amyloid diseases. Targeting these oligomers is highlighted as a promising research direction.

records.title: Atmospheric chemistry of volatile methyl siloxanes
records.description: Volatile methyl siloxanes are synthetic compounds that readily partition to the atmosphere and have been a focus of policy debates. This Review discusses advances in understanding the atmospheric chemistry, lifetimes and abundancies of these compounds and their oxidation products.

records.title: The automated red pen
records.description: Large language models can grade a stack of chemistry assignments before the kettle has boiled. Whether we should let them depends less on speed than on purpose. Before an AI marker influences grades, it should be validated like an analytical method, with defined limits, quality control and a route to appeal.

records.title: Missing marks made visible
records.description: RNA modifications shape function but are hard to localize. A recent study used an enzyme-based fluorescent method to image queuine-deficient tRNAs in cells.

records.title: The past, present and future of self-driving laboratories
records.description: Self-driving laboratories integrate automation, robotics and artificial intelligence to accelerate chemical discovery. This Review charts their evolution from bespoke systems to interoperable platforms, highlighting challenges in scalability, generalizability and data provenance, and outlining pathways towards networked, trustworthy infrastructures enabling collective scientific superintelligence.

records.title: Making sense of hydrogen evolution
records.description: Adrian Lathouwers explains how a custom glass photoreactor, which integrates an amperometric microsensor, enables controlled and reproducible hydrogen evolution measurements for assessing photocatalytic activity.

records.title: Supramolecular self-assembly by layering orthogonality to program identity, connectivity and conformation
records.description: The supramolecular self-assembly of topologically complex architectures is governed by the interplay of many reversible interaction types. This Review highlights strategies and limitations of combining different classes of interactions that must act orthogonally to direct structure. DCC, dynamic-covalent chemistry.

records.title: Physicochemical processes in evaporation-based perovskite LEDs
records.description: This Perspective presents a chemistry-driven framework linking physicochemical processes to system-level control in evaporation-based perovskite light-emitting diodes. We provide actionable guidelines for reproducible deposition and scalable device manufacturing.

records.title: Mathematics and mentorship make a recipe for success
records.description: Ahead of his 80th birthday, Isiah M. Warner, Boyd Professor Emeritus in the Department of Chemistry at Louisiana State University, discussed his life in science.

records.title: Sequence-defined polymers for predictable gene delivery
records.description: Polymer vectors for non-viral gene delivery are typically inefficient and heterogeneous. This Review explores how sequence-defined polymers, advanced synthesis, imaging and computational design can enable precise, reproducible and programmable polymer systems for efficient and clinically translatable nucleic acid delivery.

records.title: Precision chemical engineering of dendrimers for nucleic acid delivery
records.description: Dendrimers offer precise and tunable platforms for nucleic acids delivery. This Review outlines advances in dendrimer engineering for the delivery of diverse nucleic acids, highlighting their applications in therapeutics, vaccines and genome editing. Translational challenges including manufacturing, safety and regulatory considerations are also discussed, with perspectives to accelerate clinical translation.

records.title: Bridging stimulus-responsive and dissipative peptide assemblies to build complex interactive biomaterials
records.description: Self-assembling peptides offer programmable routes to biomaterials with dynamic behaviour. Here, we compare stimulus-responsive and dissipative peptide assemblies, outline their design principles, and highlight strategies to integrate them, enabling complex, interactive biomaterials that emulate the non-equilibrium functions of living systems.

records.title: Unlocking the potential of plastic in e-waste
records.description: Plastic is a rapidly growing, yet overlooked, resource of electronic waste. It should be redefined as a chemically rich feedstock for high-value materials, rather than a disposal challenge. Realizing this potential requires advances in conversion technologies, system-level process integration, and policy frameworks enabling circular materials use and resource-efficient value chains.

records.title: Devising a divisome for synthetic cells
records.description: Cell division consists of three elementary steps: symmetry breaking, membrane constriction and abscission. Here, we review current strategies for achieving these steps in synthetic cells, assessing their successes and limitations with a view to integrating them within a divisome for synthetic cells.

records.title: Feeling the force
records.description: Maria Kaeek explains the workings of a custom-built surface forces balance, a tool capable of measuring the van der Waals forces between two atomically smooth surfaces just a few nanometres apart with an unrivalled resolution.

records.title: Dyeing and drying, but not dying
records.description: In 2015, Freitag and colleagues serendipitously discovered that dye-sensitized solar cells with copper-complex electrolytes continued to function after drying out, performing as well as their liquid predecessors. This launched a new class of sold-state devices, ‘zombie’ cells, with power-conversion efficiencies over 10% in sunlight and approaching 40% under indoor light.

records.title: Tales of total synthesis
records.description: Ahead of his 80th birthday, Kyriacos Costa (K. C.) Nicolaou, Harry C. and Olga K. Wiess Professor of Chemistry at Rice University, spoke about his career in science.

records.title: A trigger that feeds itself
records.description: Most reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive prodrug linkers consume the oxidant that triggers them. A new self-immolative linker instead regenerates it, coupling drug release to signal amplification in one component.

records.title: Making chemistry sing with AI
records.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) opens up classroom creativity, enabling students and instructors to generate chemistry-themed songs with ease. This playful approach may enhance engagement, support memorization of complex concepts, and prompt critical reflection on the role of generative AI in education.

records.title: Advances in electrochemical peptide synthesis and modification
records.description: Electrochemistry is a powerful strategy for precise, tunable and sustainable synthesis that is now broadening the landscape of synthetic peptide chemistry. This Review summarizes electrochemical strategies for peptide synthesis and residue-specific modifications, highlighting opportunities for the efficient preparation of bioactive and structurally diverse peptides.

records.title: Publisher Correction: Reprogramming CO 2 reduction through interfacial water
Hydrogen generation promoted by single-atom-based thermochemical catalysts
records.description: This Review details the fundamentals of single-atom catalysts for H 2 -generation technologies. We discuss the different reaction pathways, CO x by-products and their potential eliminations, CO x -free pathways, catalyst structure–performance relationships and the techno-economics of the different processes, including cost factors and scalability.

records.title: The phonon map of molecular qubits
records.description: Molecular spin qubits are of great interest for quantum technologies due to their tunability, scalability, reproducibility and potential for room-temperature operation. While electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy is often used to study molecular qubit coherence, this has recently been paired with inelastic neutron scattering to study qubit decoherence.

records.title: Building a neuroinclusive lab
records.description: Chemistry laboratories are abundant with sensory stimuli. This Comment explores the impact of sensory overload on scientists working in these environments and offers suggestions to facilitate neuroinclusive laboratories.

records.title: Author Correction: NMR spectrometers that go places others can’t.
A career of taking biological species for a spin
records.description: Ahead of his 70th birthday, Adriaan (Ad) Bax, Distinguished Investigator at the National Institutes of Health (NIH), spoke about his career in science.

records.title: Alternating current magnetorheometer for real-time investigations
records.description: Richa Chaudhary explains how a custom alternating current magnetorheometer enables real-time rheological measurements of, for example, polymers and electromagnetic materials during exposure to alternating magnetic fields. Such measurements are not possible with conventional magnetorheometers.

records.title: Author Correction: Why university-level chemistry education in the UK is under threat
NMR spectrometers that go places others can’t
records.description: Addressing global challenges like climate change and pollution requires the development of advanced materials. To succeed, material scientists must use a diverse array of characterization tools. While often overshadowed by high-field systems, bench-top time-domain NMR offers unique advantages that could be instrumental in accelerating the development of sustainable material solutions.

records.title: Why university-level chemistry education in the UK is under threat
records.description: University-level chemistry education in the UK is facing mounting pressures that threaten its long-term viability. Without decisive intervention, we risk losing the scientific talent and capacity needed to retain the UK’s position as a leader in innovation.

records.title: Spatiotemporal analysis of reactive oxygen species using specific activity-based sensing fluorescent imaging probes
records.description: Oxidative stress arises from reactive oxygen species that are essential for signalling yet harmful when uncontrolled. Fluorescence imaging enables real-time, sensitive, organelle-level reactive oxygen species detection, and this Review outlines design principles for developing reliable probes to advance biological and medical research. MAO, monoamine oxidase; MPO, myeloperoxidase; NO, nitric oxide; NOS, nitric oxide synthase; SOD, superoxide dismutase.

records.title: Listening to the Accessible Audio Periodic Table
records.description: Every student deserves to be able to independently explore periodic trends in a chemistry course; with the Accessible Audio Periodic Table, students can now access a free tool that incorporates Universal Design for Learning (UDL) principles and accessibility to allow exploration through sound and sight.

records.title: Diversifying chemical reactions in solid oxide electrochemical cells
records.description: Nearly 40 years ago, solid oxide electrochemical cells began to evolve from supplying energy into versatile chemical reactors. Since then, breakthroughs in cell design and demonstrations of efficient value-added chemical reactions led to the exploration of how, for example, interface engineering enables more efficient and sustainable valorization reactions at reduced temperatures.

records.title: The path to understanding how reactions work and fail
records.description: Ahead of his 60th birthday, Guy Lloyd-Jones, Forbes Professor of Organic Chemistry at the University of Edinburgh, spoke about his career in science.

records.title: Fluorine-free super-repellency to water and organic liquids
records.description: Fluorine-free super-repellent materials provide sustainable and scalable alternatives to fluorinated counterparts by using re-entrant architectures or pairing non-fluorinated surface chemistries with hierarchical roughness. This Review highlights fundamental design principles, theoretical frameworks, emerging applications and future research opportunities.

records.title: Dialling in the heat
records.description: Smita Dasari explains how a radio-frequency heating apparatus can be used to, for example, cure polymers as well as probe electrical conductivities and dielectric properties of various other materials ranging from epoxies to carbon fibres and MXenes.

records.title: Light-driven reforming of methane through photothermal catalysis
records.description: This Review reframes photothermal catalytic methane reforming as a three-driving-force system, revealing how coupled photocarriers, heat (or phonons) and gradient fields govern reaction pathways, kinetics and selectivity, in addition to creating dynamic microenvironments for efficient solar-driven syngas production exemplified by dry reforming of methane.

records.title: A life researching the path to better polymers
records.description: Ahead of his 70th birthday, Takuzo Aida, Group Director at RIKEN and Distinguished University Professor at the University of Tokyo, discussed his research career.

records.title: The chemistry of magnetoelectric multiferroics
records.description: The development of ferroelectric (ferro)magnetic multiferroic materials is discussed from a chemist’s perspective, highlighting chemical contraindications, developments in solid-state chemistry that have yielded new multiferroics, chemical applications of multiferroic materials and open questions that await answers.

records.title: Polarity promotes power production
records.description: Thermoelectrochemical hydrogels can generate voltages as the temperature rises, which is often due to multiple, coupled transport mechanisms. Recent work shows how electrochemically tuning the chain-polarity can direct charge transport in hydrogels, highlighting how precise control of such chains can enhance thermoelectric performance.

records.title: Molecular rotor-based probes for protein monitoring in biomedical research
records.description: Fluorescent molecular rotor probes respond to microenvironmental changes in cells, enabling real-time, non-invasive detection of protein biomarkers in living cells, overcoming the limits of conventional approaches. They brighten upon target binding as a result of restricted intramolecular rotation and show promise for both diagnostics and research.

records.title: Chemical heterogeneity for battery materials
records.description: Materials science has long been shaped by the interplay between homogeneous and heterogeneous designs. Homogeneous battery materials offer predictability but face inherent trade-offs. Therefore, emerging research has begun to explore chemical heterogeneity to overcome these challenges and enhance the electrochemical properties of batteries.

records.title: Photochemical, electrochemical and electrophotochemical C−N bond-forming cross-coupling reactions
records.description: This Review encompasses recent developments in photochemical, electrochemical and electrophotochemical C–N coupling reactions, focusing on metal-catalysed and metal-free methodologies under diverse activation conditions. It highlights sustainable and versatile synthetic strategies for C–N bond formation.

records.title: More than just a delivery system
records.description: Lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-encapsulated messenger RNA (mRNA) vaccines proved highly effective during the COVID-19 pandemic, but how their chemical components collectively program immune responses has remained incompletely understood. Now, new work shows that both mRNA cargo and LNP materials provide layered chemical signals that instruct vaccine immunity.

records.title: Making movies with ultra-fast pair distribution functions
records.description: Adam Sapnik details the importance of custom beamline detector setups at X-ray free electron lasers for ultra-fast scattering and pair distribution function measurements of various disordered and solution-phase systems.

records.title: Light-responsive DNA nanostructures
records.description: Light-responsive chemical modifications enable precise, stimuli-controlled reconfiguration of DNA nanostructures, enhancing stability, programmability and functional versatility. These advances expand applications in diagnostics, delivery, data storage and nanoscale engineering. Emerging design strategies and new photochemical tools driving the field forward are highlighted.

records.title: Reprogramming CO 2 reduction through interfacial water
records.description: Controlling the electrochemical interface can reshape catalytic pathways. By reorganizing interfacial water with polymeric cations, CO 2 reduction on Ag shifts from CO to formic acid, revealing the importance of solvent structure for tuning electrocatalytic selectivity.

records.title: Customizing abrasives with chemical additives
records.description: Arsalan Ahmad discusses how a viscoelastic matrix composed of polymer chains, embedded with hard particles, can be used to create a custom abrasive to smoothen surfaces, cut grooves, or map pressure-points on surfaces of materials.

records.title: Author Correction: Matter in ångström-scale two-dimensional confinement
Growing pains
records.description: To write this article, the authors, members of the International Women in Supramolecular Chemistry (WISC) network surveyed colleagues who care for older children about the challenges of integrating that role with their academic careers.

records.title: Synthetic methodologies for the chemical recycling of fluorocarbons
records.description: The fluorochemical industry is extensive, but fundamentally unsustainable. In this Review, we highlight synthetic methods for recycling fluorocarbons, with a focus on methods that can be applied for industrially relevant fluorochemicals including refrigerants and fluoropolymers.

records.title: Mapping a career in electron microscopy
records.description: Ahead of his 60th birthday, Paul A. Midgley, Professor of Materials Science at the University of Cambridge, discussed his life in science.

records.title: Enhancing chemical safety information for the future
records.description: High-quality chemical safety information is essential, but information is often fragmented, inconsistent and incomplete. As a result, users face unrealistic expectations in applying risk-based principles. This article highlights persistent challenges and urges stakeholders to improve access, accuracy and application of chemical safety data.

records.title: Quantum sieving from thermal desorption
records.description: Sibo Chetry explains how an ultrahigh-vacuum chamber with a cryostat and temperature-controlled sample stage can be used for quantum sieving by thermal desorption of an isotopic mixture.

records.title: Beyond ligase logic for proteolysis
records.description: Direct recruitment of target proteins is a ubiquitination-independent approach for protein degradation and provides an alternative approach to proteolysis-targeting chimeras (PROTACs) for targeted protein degradation.

records.title: Enhancing the targeting ability of metal–organic frameworks in cancer therapy and diagnosis
records.description: This Review introduces methods for enhancing the targeting ability of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), reviews their applications when modified with different types of targeting molecules and provides guidance for the next-generation MOFs to achieve accurate cancer diagnosis and treatment.

records.title: Matter in ångström-scale two-dimensional confinement
records.description: Under confinement, matter shows different structures and behaviours, which are particularly pronounced at the ångström scale. This Review focuses on the new structures and properties of matter under such ångström-scale 2D confinement.

records.title: Catalytic droplets
records.description: A recent study showed peptides could self-assemble into catalytic droplets that could promote an aqueous aldol addition. This approach provides a proof of concept example of a droplet working as a reaction field to accelerate chemical reactions.

records.title: Tumour microenvironment in the surgical spotlight
records.description: Surgical tumour removal is often hindered by unclear margins. A recent study has developed a ‘spray on’ fluorescent probe system that rapidly stains and highlights tumour edges, enabling high contrast, real time margin detection that can be used directly in the surgical field.

records.title: Author Correction: Chemistry advances driving industrial carbon capture technologies
Understanding the degradation complexity of ultrahigh-energy lithium metal batteries
records.description: This Review discusses the lifespan failure chemistry of lithium metal batteries beyond 600 Wh kg −1 , highlighting the challenges in assessing active Li loss. We correlate material degradation, cell parameters, cell assembly and operating conditions to the overall performance and failure of a lithium metal battery.

records.title: Empowering the next generation of scientists
records.description: We are a group of graduate students from the University of California, Los Angeles who represent the Organization for Cultural Diversity in Science. In this Comment we describe a number of our initiatives to uplift and enrich the scientific community of which we are a part.

records.title: Carbon capture with COFs
records.description: A polyamine-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF) overcomes traditional direct air capture limitations with rapid CO 2 adsorption kinetics and high capacity, offering a promising solution for efficient carbon capture and sustainable climate mitigation.

records.title: Foundation models for atomistic simulation of chemistry and materials
records.description: We examine the historical development and underlying principles of foundation models realized in language and vision, and propose how physics-infused machine learning interaction potentials could dramatically transform at scale to create transformative foundation models for chemistry and materials science.

records.title: Author Correction: Substitution and electrochemistry in layered oxide cathode materials for sodium-ion batteries
A call for chemical safety and sustainability
records.description: The Stockholm Declaration on Chemistry for the Future, launched during the Nobel Symposium in May 2025, aims to align research, education, industry, and governance with the goal of focusing the future of chemistry on safety and sustainability.

records.title: A conversation with a chemical biology pioneer
records.description: Ahead of his 70th birthday, Stuart Schreiber, Morris Loeb Research Professor at Harvard University, discussed his life in science.

records.title: Towards effective and ethical GenAI in chemistry education
records.description: In 2025, chemistry education research moved towards more mature and critical uses of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI). Recent studies show how GenAI can support visualization and learning of abstract chemical concepts, while highlighting the need for strong AI literacy to manage errors, ethics and misuse.

records.title: Substitution and electrochemistry in layered oxide cathode materials for sodium-ion batteries
records.description: The impact of atomic substitution in sodium-layered oxides and how substitutions affect the properties and performances of battery materials are discussed, with the aim of improving sodium-layered oxides and accelerating the commercialization of sodium-ion batteries.

records.title: Stories from the scientist who changed how we visualize proteins
records.description: Ahead of her 85th birthday, Jane Richardson, Professor of Biochemistry at Duke University, discussed her life in science from making her own telescope to developing the ribbon diagrams for the 3D structure of proteins.

records.title: Making chemistry compute with non-steady-state chemical dynamics
records.description: Non-steady-state chemical dynamics offer a powerful tool for neuromorphic computing by harnessing nonlinear, collective, and time-evolving behaviours. Coupled with frameworks such as reservoir computing, these systems enable trajectory-based information processing at the molecular scale through concepts from chemical kinetics and far-from-equilibrium dynamics.

records.title: The geopolitical future for chemistry
records.description: In an era of global transition, new frontiers in chemistry — from space mining to circular technologies — are poised to reshape global power. This Comment explores how future supply chains, strategic resources, and chemistry could define the next era of geopolitical competition.

records.title: First-principles approaches and concepts to simulate electrochemical interfaces
records.description: State-of-the-art approaches for modelling electrified solid–electrolyte interfaces are critically discussed, highlighting key challenges in incorporating thermodynamic open-boundary conditions, large electrostatic potentials and their dynamic fluctuations into realistic ab initio simulations.

records.title: Ion migration in perovskite solar cells
records.description: Ion migration plays a crucial role in perovskite solar cells. This Review covers its mechanisms, impact on device performance and degradation, measurement techniques, and emerging strategies towards controlling ion migration.

records.title: Programming DNA machines to move
records.description: The development of DNA-based machines is transforming fields such as drug delivery and biosensing. Here, design strategies are discussed and key performance metrics — speed, force generation, efficiency and autonomy — are examined to provide insights into the future of DNA nanotechnology.

records.title: Tin, Sn!
records.description: Time flies when you’re having fun, they say. And so it is that we welcome you to the 10th volume of Nature Reviews Chemistry .

records.title: Strengthening school–university collaborations
records.description: Chemistry is an experimental science that for many learners only comes alive in the laboratory. But specialized equipment is increasingly out of reach of school budgets. Strengthening school–university collaborations can help to bridge the gap.

records.title: Biomolecular coronas govern the environmental fate of metal–organic frameworks
records.description: Metal–organic frameworks are increasingly used in environmental technologies, whereby their biomolecular coronas determine their identity, transport, persistence and ecosystem effects. We argue that further research is needed to embed corona considerations into framework systems design and regulation, and we outline the minimal, actionable steps needed to achieve this.
